edges.description: Gain-of-function FLNB cytoskeletal dysregulation in developing skeletal and joint tissues leads to congenital dislocations of the hip, knee, and elbow.
FLNB-mediated craniofacial skeletal dysplasia produces a prominent forehead as part of the characteristic facial gestalt.
FLNB-mediated craniofacial skeletal dysplasia produces a depressed nasal bridge.
FLNB-mediated craniofacial skeletal dysplasia produces widely spaced eyes (hypertelorism).
FLNB-mediated craniofacial skeletal dysplasia produces midface/malar flattening.
Altered FLNB function perturbs appendicular endochondral ossification, producing supernumerary carpal and tarsal ossification centers.
Altered FLNB function in distal limb patterning leads to short, broad, spatulate distal phalanges.
FLNB-related appendicular skeletal and joint dysplasia produces congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot).
FLNB-related vertebral and axial skeletal dysplasia produces cervical kyphosis with risk of cervical myelopathy.
FLNB-related axial skeletal and vertebral segmentation anomalies lead to kyphoscoliosis.
FLNB-related vertebral dysplasia leads to progressive scoliosis.

FLNB gain-of-function skeletal dysplasia is associated with conductive hearing impairment, though the specific middle-ear or craniofacial intermediate mechanism is not established in the cited clinical series.
Impaired chondrocyte precursor differentiation in FLNB-deficient models directly disrupts endochondral ossification and skeletal patterning.
